lens: Does every R and AC trace directly to the user's request and the confirmed Goal? Touch only what you must; out-of-scope rule violations get logged as misc-task, not fixed inline.

findings.claim: R14 + AC-16 quietly pull `scope-change/SKILL.md` into 022's change surface. The interview never authorised editing scope-change; the user signed off on a single new reviewer slot inside Gate 3 of `specflow:task`. Documenting cross-task-awareness on scope-change's E.6 re-fire path is genuine cross-task-aware work, but it belongs in a scope-change revision (or a follow-up feature), not in 022. R14's third bullet — a repository-wide grep that no other skill greps for `^### E\.5` — is also adjacent-fix scaffolding; if that grep finds a real consumer, fix it in that consumer's own feature, not here. As drafted, R14 reads like reviewer-pressure creep: a Codex finding [MAJOR] A about Phase numbering safety has been resolved by widening 022's blast radius to `scope-change/SKILL.md` and a repo-wide audit. Surgical lens fails: an R that mutates a sibling skill's body cannot trace 'directly to the user's request' when the user's request was 'add a cross-task review to task Gate 3'.
findings.evidence: PRD R14 lines 113-118 (`scope-change/SKILL.md E.6 ... document the implication`; `No other skill greps for the literal strings ^### E\.5 or Round 3 ... verified by repository-wide grep`). AC-16 lines 318-330 (`scope-change/SKILL.md`'s E.6 re-fire path is documented as cross-task-aware`). Interview Round 1 signed off on `(a) — a single new reviewer slot ... not as a re-application of existing reviewers and not as a separate gate`; Round 2 placed it inside Gate 3 of `specflow:task`. Neither round mentions scope-change. AC-16's escape hatch — `grep -qE 'cross-task|E\.4\.5' plugins/specflow/skills/scope-change/SKILL.md || grep -qE ... plugins/specflow/templates/task/cross-task-review.md` — already shows the author noticed the surface mismatch and tried to absorb it into the doctrine doc; that disjunction is the correct answer. Make it the only answer.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the scope-change/SKILL.md edit from R14's surface entirely. Rewrite R14 as: (1) Phase E.4.5 numbering insertion is internal to `task/SKILL.md` and need not propagate; (2) the cross-task doctrine doc at `templates/task/cross-task-review.md` documents how scope-change's E.6 re-fire interacts with Phase E.4.5 (one paragraph; no scope-change edit); (3) remove the `repository-wide grep` audit clause — if it finds nothing, it added zero requirements; if it finds something, log a misc-task per the surgical principle and ship 022 without that cleanup. Tighten AC-16 to the doctrine-doc check only: `grep -qE 'cross-task|E\.4\.5' plugins/specflow/templates/task/cross-task-review.md` AND `grep -qE 'tasks-gate3/manifest\.md' plugins/specflow/skills/brief/SKILL.md` (compatibility verification, no edit). Drop the scope-change disjunction. If a future scope-change author needs to know about Phase E.4.5, the doctrine doc is where they look; that's chain-don't-absorb working as intended.

findings.claim: R7's `agent_id` mechanism ships substrate the future 027 must absorb — but the PRD itself flags this as a Non-goal (`Building 027-reviewer-context-isolation itself ... 027 absorbs/extends. Goal-level out-of-scope`). The Non-goals list rules 027 OUT, then R7 implements a three-field ID schema, a generation convention (`writer-{ISO-8601-timestamp}-{4-hex-suffix}`, `xtr-{round}-{ISO-8601-timestamp}-{4-hex-suffix}`, `applier-{ISO-8601-timestamp}-{4-hex-suffix}`), an echo-back protocol, a manifest-side consistency check, AND a `FRESH-CONTEXT-VIOLATION` escalation surface. That's not 'an interim manifest field' — that's a fresh-context audit contract with a defined wire format. The interview Round 8 user-deferred-to-AI's-better-judgement; the AI took that latitude and built 027's foundation inside 022. A surgical 022 ships ONE field — `cross_task_reviewer_id` — not three; the goal-level success criterion is `manifest's writer_id ≠ cross_task_reviewer_id` (interview line 12), not a three-way fresh-context-violation detector. The `applier_id` only matters if you're building 027; in 022 the applier's identity is implicit (it's `specflow:task --apply-cross-task-feedback` re-invocation; no audit field needed for 022's success criterion).
findings.evidence: PRD Non-goals line 32 (`Building 027-reviewer-context-isolation itself ... 022 ships the interim agent_id mechanism + forked-sub-agent dispatch convention; 027 absorbs/extends. (Goal-level out-of-scope.)`) directly contradicts R7 lines 80-87 (which spec the absorbed contract). The interview's Goal § Success looks like (line 25) names ONE auditable signal: `the manifest's writer_id differs from the cross_task_reviewer_id`. There is no interview round naming `applier_id` as a success criterion; Round 8 only mentions `writer_id ≠ cross_task_reviewer_id ≠ applier_id` as Resolved-text the AI synthesised after `User: deferred to AI's better judgement` — that's exactly the latitude that produces scope creep. The PRD's `FRESH-CONTEXT-VIOLATION` escalation surface (line 85) is a 027-shaped contract; 022's interim is supposed to be a `field` per Round 8.
findings.proposed_change: Strip R7 down to: `Gate 3 manifest gains a single best-effort field cross_task_reviewer_id, populated at E.4.5.1 dispatch with the value the orchestrator passes in its dispatch brief (the reviewer echoes it back in the finding JSON's top-level field). The closer records the echoed value verbatim. The closing-decision footer notes if writer_id (already implicit in the originating specflow:task run timestamp) and cross_task_reviewer_id are identical, in which case the manifest carries one info-level note. No FRESH-CONTEXT-VIOLATION escalation surface in 022 — that's 027's contract.` Drop applier_id from the manifest; it becomes a 027 addition. Drop the `xtr-{round}-...` and `applier-...` schemes; 027 owns ID format. Update AC-7 + AC-15 + AC-13 (eval clause 2) accordingly: AC-7 checks one field, AC-15 checks `writer_id ≠ cross_task_reviewer_id` only, AC-13's eval clause 2 drops the `applier_id` reference. This collapses R7 from 8 lines to 2-3, matches the interview's signed-off success criterion exactly, and leaves 027 a clean substrate to define.

findings.claim: The Goals section grew from the interview's signed-off ask. Interview Goal (lines 22-27) describes: a whole-set cross-task review with two lenses, fresh context, manifest finding, worked example. The PRD's Goals (lines 19-28) ships nine bullets, several of which are mechanism-spec rather than goals: 'three-round mini-debate inside Round 2.5' (R3 mechanism), 'Add writer_id, cross_task_reviewer_id, and applier_id fields' (R7 mechanism), 'Auto-route PRD-coverage-changing cross-task findings ... auto-apply' (R6 mechanism), 'Surface within-budget merge/split signals from context-budget-estimate' (R9 mechanism). Goals should answer 'what does success look like?' not 'how is it built?'. Mixing mechanism into Goals inflates the apparent surface and makes downstream 'serves goal' Trace lines on R1-R15 look more grounded than they are — every R can find SOME Goal bullet to cite when Goals double as a mechanism inventory. Surgical lens: every changed line should trace to the user's request; when Goals = mechanism, the trace becomes circular.
findings.evidence: Compare PRD Goals lines 22, 24, 25, 26 (each is a how, not a what) against interview Goal lines 23-27 (each is a what — outcome / audience / success-looks-like / driving value). The PRD's own R3 Trace cites `Outcome (three-round convergence with forced decision after three rounds)` — but 'three-round convergence' isn't an outcome, it's a mechanism. The user-facing outcome is 'cross-task findings reach the manifest with a forced decision after three rounds'; the three-round structure is the means.
findings.proposed_change: Collapse Goals to four bullets that match the interview's Outcome / Audience / Success-looks-like / Driving-value structure: (1) `specflow:task` Gate 3 gains a whole-set cross-task review alongside per-task review, with two lenses (coherence + better-arrangement); (2) Engineer + admin + downstream-skill audiences see cross-task findings in a dedicated manifest section, lens-distinguished from per-task; (3) Success: a fresh feature run produces a Gate 3 manifest with both finding types; the worked example demonstrates one coherence + one better-arrangement finding surfaced + resolved; (4) Driving value: closes Pocock's whole-set lens gap that per-task reviewers can't see. Move the three-round mini-debate, the agent_id field, the auto-routing, and the budget-soft-signal into Requirements where they're already documented (R3 / R7 / R6 / R9 respectively). The Goals section gets back to ~8 lines and the 'serves goal' Trace lines on R1-R15 carry honest weight.

findings.claim: R15 promotes `--apply-cross-task-feedback` to a `first-class mode entry-point` with explicit Inputs-section branch + Phase A Resume-logic branch. The interview Round 6 calls it `a new mode/flag (e.g. specflow:task --apply-cross-task-feedback {NNN-slug})` — a single sentence about how the applier is invoked, no mention of Inputs documentation or Resume-branch surgery. R15 is reviewer-pressure creep from Codex finding [MAJOR] B; the actual user surface is internal (the orchestrator calls the applier as a forked sub-skill, not a user typing the flag at a prompt). Surgical change here is a one-liner under R5 documenting the flag; rewriting Inputs + Phase A Resume logic to make it 'first-class' is over-engineering for a programmatically-invoked subroutine.
findings.evidence: Interview Round 6 line 67 (`a new mode/flag (e.g. specflow:task --apply-cross-task-feedback {NNN-slug})`) — single mention, no UX requirement. PRD R15 lines 120-122 specs `task/SKILL.md § Inputs (currently lines 31-36) gains an explicit branch documenting the new mode flag — alongside the existing specflow:task {NNN} and /specflow:task entries`. The existing Inputs section is for *user* entry points; the applier flag is invoked by the orchestrator (see R5: `specflow:task is re-invoked in a fresh context window`). AC-17 lines 333-343 then requires both the Inputs grep AND the Phase-A Resume-branch grep — two SKILL-body edits for what is effectively an orchestrator-side detail.
findings.proposed_change: Demote R15 to a clarification under R5: `R5 also: Phase A's resume-detection skips its verify-the-artefact-chain step when invoked with --apply-cross-task-feedback (the chain is verified by the parent Gate 3 invocation that triggered the applier). The flag is documented in Phase F's preamble, not in the user-facing Inputs section.` Drop AC-17 entirely (or fold its second clause — the Phase A jump-to-F branch — into AC-5's existing Phase F existence check). This drops two SKILL-body edits and one AC, and matches the interview's actual surface: the flag exists, it's used by the orchestrator, that's it.

findings.claim: R10's `Ordering guarantee` clause re-runs Phase B.4 (coverage-matrix verification) after the applier's final pass, before E.5 starts. This is a defensive belt-AND-suspenders: the applier already runs B.4-equivalent coverage checks (it's `specflow:task` re-invoked, which inherits B.4 logic per R5's 'applier inherits synthesis logic for free'). Codex finding [MAJOR] E asked for an ordering guarantee; the surgical answer is `E.4.5.4 must complete before E.5` (one sentence). Adding a B.4 re-run + a `B4-CHECK-FAILED-POST-APPLIER` diagnostic creates a second failure mode the user has to interpret, for the case where the applier's own coverage logic missed something — but if the applier's coverage logic is unreliable, that's an applier bug, not a Gate 3 ordering issue.
findings.evidence: PRD R10 lines 99-103 (`Phase E.4.5.4 (applier final pass) must complete writing the post-applier tasks.md AND re-run Phase B.4 self-check (coverage matrix verification) BEFORE Phase E.5 (per-task sharpen) starts. If B.4 fails after the applier's final pass, the gate halts with a B4-CHECK-FAILED-POST-APPLIER diagnostic`). R5 line 72 specs the applier as `specflow:task re-invoked in a fresh context window`; the applier already runs Phase B.4 as part of its inherited synthesis logic. The doubled check is overhead.
findings.proposed_change: Trim R10's second paragraph to: `Ordering guarantee: Phase E.4.5.4 must complete writing the post-applier tasks.md before Phase E.5 starts. Phase E.5 reads the post-applier tasks.md as its input; if the applier wrote an incomplete file, per-task reviewers will surface the issue in their normal lens.` Drop the `B4-CHECK-FAILED-POST-APPLIER` diagnostic surface. AC-10 stays as-is (it only checks ordering). This honours the Codex ordering finding without adding a new failure-mode surface.
